assumptions.landscape: Corn and soybeans, Story County, Iowa. Both crops mature by late September and dry down standing in the field; soybean harvest runs late September to mid October, corn harvest October into early November. Residue burning is rare here, so burn_scar and fire will mostly read clear.
assumptions.season_start: The pipeline season starts 2026-06-01 (frames available from then). Peak greenness in late July is still captured; an April start would add the bare-soil baseline but needs the cube re-pulled.
assumptions.sowing_window_days: ASSUMPTION: days after the combine to drill a cover crop (cereal rye) or finish fall tillage. Only the dispatch extension uses it as a deadline.
assumptions.machine_rate_ha_per_day: ASSUMPTION ~100 acres/day for one combine (12-row corn head or 35 ft platform). Dispatch extension only; the morning plans do not use it.
assumptions.share_needing_chc: ASSUMPTION: share of row-crop area combined by a custom operator rather than an owned machine; most Iowa operations own a combine, 15% is a scenario placeholder. Dispatch extension only.
assumptions.baseline_request_lag_days: ASSUMPTION: a custom operator is booked about 2 days after the field is judged ready. Dispatch extension only.
assumptions.max_service_km: ASSUMPTION: custom crews work a county-scale radius; 40 km covers the whole box from any simulated depot in config/chcs.json.
assumptions.thresholds: harvest_ndvi_max 0.25 separates residue (about 0.15 to 0.25) from dry standing corn and soybeans (about 0.25 to 0.40): on synthetic corn/soy seasons the old 0.35 called more than half the standing fields harvested weeks early. To be checked against real fields and USDA Crop Progress (intelligence/validate_usda.py). No sown_ndvi_min: no following crop inside the window, so the regrow check is off. frost_tmin_c: a forecast minimum at or below it within the rain lookahead triggers harvest-versus-weather on a ready crop; needs forecast tmin_c in weather.json.
assumptions.crop_system: corn_soy drives the mock generator (field sizes, dry-down phenology, rare burning, autumn frost) and nothing else; the models themselves are crop-agnostic. rice_wheat is the Punjab stand-in.
